target: Apa pun yang terjadi besok, kami tetap berangkat pagi-pagi.
english: Whatever happens tomorrow, we are still leaving early in the morning.
grammar: Pun is written separately after question words: apa pun = anything/whatever, siapa pun = anyone.

target: Siapa pun boleh ikut kelas memasak ini tanpa mendaftar dulu.
english: Anyone may join this cooking class without registering first.

target: Kapan pun kamu butuh bantuan, telepon saja saya.
english: Whenever you need help, just call me.

target: Di mana pun kami makan, adik selalu memesan mi goreng.
english: Wherever we eat, my little brother always orders fried noodles.
grammar: Di mana pun = wherever: di mana pun kami makan = wherever we eat.

target: Ke mana pun dia pindah, buku-buku lamanya selalu ikut dibawa.
english: Wherever he moves, his old books always get brought along.

target: Saya tidak membawa uang tunai satu lembar pun hari ini.
english: I am not carrying even a single bill of cash today.
grammar: With a negative, satu + noun + pun = not even one: satu lembar pun = not even one bill.

target: Dia tidak menjawab satu pertanyaan pun dalam wawancara tadi.
english: He did not answer even one question in the interview earlier.

target: Saya belum pernah terlambat sekali pun selama bekerja di sini.
english: I have never been late even once while working here.
grammar: Sekali pun (two words) = even once: belum terlambat sekali pun = never late, not even once.

target: Bahkan hujan deras pun tidak membatalkan pertandingan sore itu.
english: Even the heavy rain did not cancel the match that afternoon.

target: Turis asing pun sering ikut upacara bendera di desa kami.
english: Even foreign tourists often join the flag ceremony in our village.

target: Jangan menyerah, sesulit apa pun soal ujiannya.
english: Don't give up, no matter how difficult the exam questions are.
grammar: Se- + adjective + apa pun = no matter how: sesulit apa pun = no matter how difficult.

target: Dia berangkat tanpa pamit kepada siapa pun di rumah.
english: He left without saying goodbye to anyone at home.
grammar: Tanpa ... siapa pun = without anyone at all: tanpa pamit kepada siapa pun.

target: Kata dokter, ayah tidak boleh minum kopi sedikit pun dulu.
english: According to the doctor, Dad may not drink even a little coffee for now.

target: Kapan pun ada diskon besar, toko itu langsung ramai.
english: Whenever there is a big sale, that store immediately gets crowded.

target: Apa pun menunya, masakan nenek selalu habis duluan.
english: Whatever is on the menu, Grandma's cooking always runs out first.

target: Bahkan anak-anak kecil di kampung ini bisa berenang di sungai.
english: Even the small children in this village can swim in the river.

target: Harga cabai naik terus, bahkan pedagang pun ikut mengeluh.
english: Chili prices keep rising; even the vendors are complaining too.
grammar: Bahkan = even, introduces the strongest example: bahkan pedagang pun = even the vendors.

target: Dia hafal semua nama pelanggan, bahkan nama anak-anak mereka.
english: She knows all the customers' names by heart, even their children's names.

target: Kakak saya rajin sekali; bahkan pada hari libur dia tetap bangun jam lima.
english: My older brother is very diligent; even on days off he still gets up at five.

target: Bahkan setelah dua kali dijelaskan, saya masih bingung dengan aturan pajak ini.
english: Even after it was explained twice, I am still confused by these tax rules.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh, bahkan pada Selasa malam.
english: That restaurant is always full, even on Tuesday nights.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini panjang, bahkan bulan Juni masih sering banjir.
english: The rainy season this year is long; even in June it still floods often.

target: Dia belum pernah ke Bali, bahkan belum pernah naik pesawat sama sekali.
english: He has never been to Bali; in fact he has never even been on a plane at all.

target: Bahkan bos kami ikut membantu mengangkat kursi untuk acara besok.
english: Even our boss joined in helping carry the chairs for tomorrow's event.

target: Ibu ingat semua tanggal penting, bahkan tanggal pernikahan tetangga.
english: Mom remembers all the important dates, even the neighbors' wedding date.

target: Saya cuma mau memastikan jadwal rapat besok tidak berubah.
english: I just want to make sure tomorrow's meeting schedule hasn't changed.
grammar: Cuma = only/just, the everyday spoken word; hanya means the same but sounds more careful.

target: Tenang, ini cuma latihan, bukan gempa sungguhan.
english: Relax, this is only a drill, not a real earthquake.
grammar: Cuma X, bukan Y contrasts: cuma latihan, bukan gempa = just a drill, not an earthquake.

target: Kami cuma punya waktu lima belas menit sebelum toko tutup.
english: We only have fifteen minutes before the store closes.

target: Dia cuma bercanda, jangan diambil hati.
english: He is only joking, don't take it to heart.

target: Hanya penumpang dengan tiket kelas satu yang boleh masuk ruang tunggu ini.
english: Only passengers with first-class tickets may enter this waiting lounge.
grammar: Hanya X yang ... = only X (and no one else): hanya penumpang ini yang boleh masuk.

target: Hadiah ini hanya untuk pelanggan yang belanja di atas seratus ribu.
english: This gift is only for customers who spend over one hundred thousand.

target: Dari semua lamaran itu, hanya tiga orang yang dipanggil wawancara.
english: Out of all those applications, only three people were called for an interview.

target: Saya cuma sempat sarapan roti tawar sebelum berangkat tadi pagi.
english: I only had time to eat plain bread for breakfast before leaving this morning.

target: Obat ini hanya boleh diminum setelah makan, ya.
english: This medicine may only be taken after eating, okay?

target: Masalahnya cuma satu: kami belum menemukan tempat parkir yang aman.
english: There is only one problem: we haven't found a safe parking spot yet.

target: Hanya karena satu ulasan buruk, dia hampir menutup warungnya.
english: Just because of one bad review, she almost closed her food stall.

target: Cuma orang sabar yang tahan mengantre selama itu.
english: Only patient people can stand queuing that long.

target: Kamu bisa datang kapan saja, pintu rumah kami selalu terbuka.
english: You can come any time; the door of our house is always open.
grammar: Question word + saja = any-: kapan saja = anytime, apa saja = anything, siapa saja = anyone.

target: Ambil kue mana saja yang kamu suka dari meja itu.
english: Take whichever cake you like from that table.

target: Di kota besar, makanan apa saja bisa dipesan lewat aplikasi.
english: In a big city, any food can be ordered through an app.

target: Siapa saja boleh menyumbang buku untuk perpustakaan kecil kami.
english: Anyone may donate books to our little library.

target: Dia pergi begitu saja tanpa meninggalkan pesan apa pun.
english: He left just like that without leaving any message at all.
grammar: Begitu saja = just like that: pergi begitu saja = left just like that, no explanation.

target: Jangan percaya begitu saja pada berita yang belum jelas sumbernya.
english: Don't just blindly believe news whose source isn't clear yet.

target: Kami baru saja membicarakan proyek itu ketika listrik mati.
english: We had just been discussing that project when the electricity went out.

target: Adik baru saja tidur, tolong kecilkan suara televisinya.
english: The little one just fell asleep; please turn the TV volume down.
grammar: Baru saja = just (moments ago): baru saja tidur = just fell asleep.

target: Anggap saja rumah sendiri, jangan malu-malu.
english: Just treat it like your own home, don't be shy.
grammar: Anggap saja = just consider it: anggap saja rumah sendiri = make yourself at home.

target: Kalau bingung, tanya saja petugas di pintu masuk.
english: If you're confused, just ask the staff at the entrance.

target: Sisanya bungkus saja, sayang kalau dibuang.
english: Just wrap up the leftovers; it would be a waste to throw them away.

target: Perasaan saya saja, atau ruangan ini memang lebih dingin dari biasanya?
english: Is it just my imagination, or is this room really colder than usual?
grammar: X saja can mean 'it's just (my) X': perasaan saya saja = it's just my imagination.

target: Undangannya lewat pesan singkat saja, tidak perlu mencetak kartu.
english: The invitations can just go by text message; there's no need to print cards.

target: Tulis saja dulu semua ide yang muncul, kita bisa memilihnya nanti.
english: Just write down all the ideas that come up first; we can choose among them later.

target: Baru saja kami membahas cara hemat listrik, tiba-tiba lampu kantor padam.
english: We had just been discussing how to save electricity when suddenly the office lights went out.

target: Santai saja, hasil tesnya baru keluar minggu depan.
english: Just relax; the test results only come out next week.

target: Setelah tiga kali gagal, akhirnya dia lulus ujian menyetir juga.
english: After failing three times, he finally passed the driving test at last.
grammar: Akhirnya ... juga = finally, at last: akhirnya lulus juga = finally passed (after all that).

target: Sudah jam sembilan malam, paket saya belum diantar juga.
english: It's already nine at night and my package still hasn't been delivered.
grammar: Belum ... juga = STILL not: belum diantar juga = still hasn't been delivered.

target: Ternyata kamu suka kopi tanpa gula juga, sama seperti saya.
english: It turns out you like coffee without sugar too, just like me.

target: Selain murah, kos ini dekat stasiun juga.
english: Besides being cheap, this boarding house is close to the station too.

target: Dipikir-pikir, tinggal di kota kecil enak juga.
english: Come to think of it, living in a small town is actually pretty nice.
grammar: Juga can soften an opinion: enak juga = actually pretty nice (a mild, pleasant surprise).

target: Kalau kamu ikut, saya ikut juga.
english: If you're going, I'm going too.

target: Ternyata belajar bahasa baru itu melelahkan juga.
english: It turns out learning a new language is actually tiring.

target: Dia bukan hanya pintar memasak, tetapi pintar mengatur uang juga.
english: She is not only good at cooking, but good at managing money too.
grammar: Bukan hanya X, tetapi Y juga = not only X but also Y.

target: Ditunggu sampai sore, tukang ledengnya tidak datang juga.
english: We waited until the afternoon, but the plumber still didn't come.

target: Anak bungsu kami akhirnya berani tampil di panggung juga.
english: Our youngest child finally dared to perform on stage after all.

target: Setelah dibujuk lama, kakek mau memakai kursi roda juga.
english: After much persuading, Grandpa was finally willing to use the wheelchair.

target: Harga bensin naik, jadi ongkos ojek naik juga.
english: Fuel prices went up, so motorcycle-taxi fares went up too.

target: Katanya sedang diet, tapi dia memesan es krim juga.
english: She says she's on a diet, but she ordered ice cream anyway.

target: Pelan-pelan, akhirnya bahasa Indonesianya lancar juga.
english: Little by little, his Indonesian finally became fluent after all.

target: Sejak kuliah di luar kota, dia belajar mengatur uangnya sendiri.
english: Since studying in another city, she has learned to manage her money by herself.
grammar: Sendiri after a verb phrase = by oneself: mengatur uangnya sendiri = manage her money herself.

target: Jangan hanya percaya cerita orang, coba buktikan sendiri.
english: Don't just believe other people's stories; try to prove it yourself.

target: Kami membangun rumah kecil ini sendiri selama dua tahun.
english: We built this little house ourselves over two years.

target: Nenek masih mencuci bajunya sendiri walaupun sudah ada mesin cuci.
english: Grandma still washes her clothes herself even though there is a washing machine.

target: Lampu teras itu mati sendiri setiap tengah malam.
english: That porch light turns off by itself every midnight.
grammar: Sendiri can mean 'by itself': mati sendiri = went off on its own, nobody touched it.

target: Setiap karyawan bertanggung jawab atas meja kerjanya sendiri.
english: Every employee is responsible for his or her own desk.
grammar: Noun + -nya sendiri = one's own: meja kerjanya sendiri = his own desk.

target: Dia lebih suka bepergian sendiri karena bebas mengatur jadwal.
english: He prefers traveling alone because he is free to set his own schedule.

target: Anak itu sudah bisa memakai sepatunya sendiri sejak umur tiga tahun.
english: That child has been able to put on her own shoes since age three.

target: Saya suka masakan pedas, tetapi suami saya punya selera sendiri.
english: I like spicy food, but my husband has his own taste.

target: Pintu garasi itu bisa menutup sendiri kalau tidak ditahan.
english: That garage door can close by itself if it isn't held.

target: Sejak SMA, kakak sudah punya penghasilan sendiri dari mengajar les.
english: Since high school, my older sister has had her own income from tutoring.

target: Dia memilih tinggal sendiri supaya lebih fokus menulis bukunya.
english: He chose to live alone so he could focus more on writing his book.

target: Kami menanam sayur sendiri di belakang rumah sejak tahun lalu.
english: We have been growing our own vegetables behind the house since last year.

target: Setelah rapat, kami kembali ke ruangan masing-masing.
english: After the meeting, we returned to our respective rooms.
grammar: Masing-masing = each/respective: ruangan masing-masing = each person's own room.

target: Peserta lomba membawa alat masak masing-masing dari rumah.
english: The contest participants bring their own cooking utensils from home.

target: Setiap daerah punya cara masing-masing untuk merayakan panen.
english: Every region has its own way of celebrating the harvest.

target: Anak-anak menyimpan uang jajan masing-masing di celengan.
english: The children keep their own pocket money in piggy banks.

target: Masing-masing kelompok mendapat waktu sepuluh menit untuk presentasi.
english: Each group gets ten minutes for the presentation.

target: Kami membayar tiket masing-masing supaya tidak repot menghitung nanti.
english: We each pay for our own tickets so we don't have the hassle of calculating later.

target: Silakan isi formulir sesuai data masing-masing.
english: Please fill in the form according to your own information.

target: Dua koki itu terkenal dengan resep sambal masing-masing.
english: Those two chefs are famous for their respective sambal recipes.

target: Hotelnya bersih, murah, dan dekat pantai pula.
english: The hotel is clean, cheap, and close to the beach as well.
grammar: Pula = 'as well/what's more' — a slightly bookish juga: dekat pantai pula = close to the beach too.

target: Dia datang terlambat, tanpa membawa laporan pula.
english: He arrived late, and without bringing the report, no less.

target: Jalan menuju air terjun itu jauh, licin pula ketika hujan.
english: The path to that waterfall is far, and slippery too when it rains.

target: Ujian ini panjang, sulit pula, jadi siapkan tenaga.
english: This exam is long, and difficult as well, so get your energy ready.

target: Harganya naik dua kali lipat, stoknya terbatas pula.
english: The price doubled, and the stock is limited as well.

target: Anak itu rajin, sopan pula kepada semua guru.
english: That child is diligent, and polite to all the teachers as well.

target: Kemarin dia lupa dompet, hari ini lupa kunci pula.
english: Yesterday he forgot his wallet; today he forgot his keys as well.

target: Acaranya mulai malam, tempatnya jauh pula, jadi kami menginap di sana.
english: The event starts at night, and the venue is far too, so we are staying over there.

target: Memang saya yang salah kemarin, dan saya sudah minta maaf.
english: It really was me who was wrong yesterday, and I have already apologized.
grammar: Memang = indeed/admittedly, confirms a fact: memang saya yang salah = it really was my fault.

target: Kereta ekonomi memang lebih lambat, tetapi pemandangannya indah.
english: The economy train is indeed slower, but the scenery is beautiful.

target: Kamu benar, durian memang bukan buah untuk semua orang.
english: You're right, durian is indeed not a fruit for everyone.

target: Dia memang jarang bicara, tapi kalau bicara isinya selalu penting.
english: He indeed rarely speaks, but when he does, what he says is always important.

target: Rumah di pinggir sawah itu memang terlihat tenang.
english: The house at the edge of the rice field does look peaceful.

target: Memang benar kata ibu, membawa payung itu tidak pernah rugi.
english: Mom was right indeed: bringing an umbrella never hurts.

target: Pekerjaan di dapur restoran memang berat, apalagi saat akhir pekan.
english: Work in a restaurant kitchen is indeed hard, especially on weekends.

target: Soal macet, kota ini memang juaranya.
english: When it comes to traffic jams, this city is truly the champion.
grammar: Soal X = when it comes to X: soal macet = as for traffic jams.

target: Saya memang belum lama kenal dia, tapi saya percaya dia jujur.
english: I admittedly haven't known him long, but I believe he is honest.

target: Ongkos hidup di ibu kota memang tinggi, tetapi gajinya juga lebih tinggi.
english: The cost of living in the capital is indeed high, but the salaries are also higher.

target: Filmnya bagus sih, cuma terlalu panjang untuk saya.
english: The movie is good, I admit, it's just too long for me.
grammar: Sih adds a casual spoken nuance you will hear everywhere: bagus sih = it's good, I admit.

target: Motor ini bisa diparkir di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan.
english: This motorbike can be parked anywhere as long as it doesn't block the road.
grammar: Asal = as long as: di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan = anywhere, provided it doesn't block.

target: Sekecil apa pun sumbangannya, panitia pasti mencatat dengan rapi.
english: No matter how small the donation, the committee will definitely record it neatly.

target: Kami tidak menyangka kamu datang jauh-jauh hanya untuk makan bakso.
english: We didn't expect you to come all this way just to eat meatballs.

target: Bahkan di musim liburan, pantai ini tetap sepi dan bersih.
english: Even in the holiday season, this beach stays quiet and clean.

target: Undian ini terbuka untuk siapa saja, termasuk karyawan baru.
english: This prize draw is open to anyone, including new employees.

target: Saya sendiri belum pernah mencoba durian goreng itu.
english: I myself have never tried that fried durian.
grammar: Pronoun + sendiri = myself/himself (emphasis): saya sendiri = I myself.

target: Bapak kos kami memang baik; bahkan sering mengantar tamu ke stasiun.
english: Our landlord is truly kind; he even often takes guests to the station.

target: Musim kemarau pun, sumur di desa ini tidak pernah kering.
english: Even in the dry season, the well in this village never runs dry.
grammar: Noun + pun = even: musim kemarau pun = even (in) the dry season.

target: Dia menghabiskan akhir pekan hanya untuk menonton ulang serial lama.
english: He spent the weekend just rewatching an old series.

target: Kalian berdua saja yang berangkat duluan, saya menyusul nanti.
english: Just the two of you go ahead first; I'll follow later.
grammar: Berdua saja = just the two (of you/us): kalian berdua saja = just you two.

target: Setiap pagi dia menyapu halaman rumahnya sendiri sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: Every morning he sweeps his own front yard before leaving for work.

target: Tiket konser itu habis dalam lima menit saja.
english: The concert tickets sold out in just five minutes.
grammar: Number + saja = just/only that much: lima menit saja = in a mere five minutes.

target: Bukan cuma anak-anak, orang dewasa juga suka taman hiburan ini.
english: It's not just kids; adults like this amusement park too.

target: Berita itu memang mengejutkan, tetapi kami mencoba tetap tenang.
english: The news was indeed shocking, but we tried to stay calm.

target: Masing-masing pihak sudah menandatangani surat perjanjian sewa.
english: Each party has signed the rental agreement.

target: Jangankan naik gunung, jalan ke warung pun dia malas.
english: Let alone climbing a mountain; he's too lazy even to walk to the food stall.
grammar: Jangankan X, Y pun ... = let alone X, even Y: jangankan lari, jalan pun malas.

target: Kami berdua memesan menu yang sama, minumannya saja yang berbeda.
english: The two of us ordered the same dish; only the drinks were different.
grammar: X saja yang ... = only X (is what differs): minumannya saja yang berbeda = only the drinks differ.

target: Pelan tapi pasti, usaha kecilnya akhirnya dikenal orang juga.
english: Slowly but surely, his small business finally became known to people after all.
